title: The imec Report: Advancing The CFET-Based Device Roadmap
gist: imec lays out its case that complementary FET (CFET) architectures will enter the logic roadmap from the A7 node onward, enabling 4.5-track and eventually 3-track standard cells and extending classical CMOS to at least A3. It reports two 2026 VLSI results: a new backside-contact scheme with frontside plus backside dielectric isolation that raises bottom pFET drive current fivefold, cuts access resistance from 1753 to 378 ohm-micron and lifts device survival yield from 45% to 85%; and a 'dipole-middle' gate-stack integration that delivers multi-Vt tuning at a thermal budget compatible with monolithic CFET's low-temperature replacement metal gate flow.

themes.theme: Logic roadmap and node transition timing

insights.claim: GAA nanosheet transistors are expected to carry scaling only down to the A10 logic generation, where they enable 5.5-track standard cells, setting a concrete architectural ceiling on the current transistor generation.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Anchors when foundries must commit capital to a new device architecture; A10 is the last node where nanosheet tooling and IP investment fully amortizes.
insights.quote: GAA nanosheet transistor technology offers scalability down to the A10 logic generation, where it enables 5.5-track (T) standard cells

insights.claim: From the A7 node onward the industry is likely to transition to CFET-based transistor architectures, which enable 4.5-track and below standard cells.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Dates the next device-architecture inflection for equipment, EDA and IP roadmaps — A7 is the node where CFET-specific process modules and cell libraries must already exist.
insights.quote: From the A7 logic technology node onwards, industry may likely transition to CFET-based transistor architectures which enable 4.5-track (4.5T) and below standard cells.

insights.claim: Stacking pMOS on nMOS via CFET can push standard cells down to 3 tracks, extending the classical CMOS logic roadmap to at least the A3 technology node.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Puts a floor under the 'end of Moore's Law' narrative — classical CMOS scaling has a credible technical path several nodes beyond A7.
insights.quote: standard cells can be further scaled down to 3T, thereby extending the classical CMOS logic roadmap to at least the A3 technology node
insights.locator: For the A7 node, options are becoming

insights.claim: At A7 the roadmap forks into at least three competing options — imec's CMOS 2.0 heterogeneous-tier partitioning, pushing GAA nanosheet to its ultimate scaling limits with frontside or backside power, or transitioning to CFET — so there is no single consensus successor architecture.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Divergent roadmaps at A7 mean foundry differentiation and higher tooling uncertainty; suppliers exposed to only one path carry more risk than those selling into all three.
insights.quote: options are becoming increasingly diverse to meet the growing diversification of application needs, driven by the AI revolution
insights.locator: For the A7 node, options are becoming

insights.claim: imec attributes the diversification of node options directly to the AI revolution's diversification of application needs, framing workload specialization — not lithography — as the driver of roadmap branching.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Supports a thesis that leading-edge capacity fragments across workload-specific process options, favoring foundries with broad option menus over pure single-flow scale.
insights.locator: For the A7 node, options are becoming

insights.claim: Under the CMOS 2.0 paradigm an SoC is partitioned into heterogeneous functional tiers, each built in the most suitable technology and reconnected with 3D interconnect — making 3D interconnect capability, not transistor density alone, the gating capability for the next generation of SoCs.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Reinforces the strategic value of hybrid bonding, wafer bonding and 3D stacking suppliers as an alternative scaling vector to the transistor itself.
insights.quote: a system-on-chip (SoC) is partitioned into heterogeneous, functional tiers each optimized using the most suitable technology, and reconnected using 3D interconnect technologies

insights.claim: Monolithic CFET is believed to offer the fastest path to industrial adoption, with sequential CFET dependent on further progress in alignment accuracy.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Directs where process-equipment demand lands first: mCFET favors high-aspect-ratio patterning and selective deposition/etch over the bonding-and-alignment toolset sCFET requires.
insights.quote: Pending further progress in alignment accuracy, mCFET is believed to offer the fastest path to industrial adoption.
insights.locator: Both approaches start from the vertical stacking

insights.claim: Sequential CFET's individual process steps are simpler than monolithic CFET's, but some critical steps must be run twice and the flow involves two wafer flips that distort the wafer and challenge precise front-to-back alignment — a clean cost/complexity tradeoff between the two approaches.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Wafer distortion during flips is the specific technical gate on sCFET; overlay metrology and bonding-alignment vendors are the direct beneficiaries if it is solved.
insights.quote: sCFET additionally involves two wafer flips, distorting the wafer and challenging the precise alignment of front-to-back device connections.
insights.locator: Both approaches start from the vertical stacking

insights.claim: Monolithic CFET requires patterning, deposition and selective removal of materials around and between a high-aspect-ratio device structure in a single process sequence, concentrating the difficulty in module development rather than in step count.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Selective-removal and area-selective deposition chemistries become the differentiating capability at CFET nodes — a specialty-materials and etch opportunity.
insights.locator: Both approaches start from the vertical stacking

insights.claim: Both monolithic and sequential CFET start from the same vertical Si/SiGe layer stack from which n and pFETs are fabricated, so epitaxy capability is a shared prerequisite regardless of which integration path wins.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Epi tool and precursor suppliers are the path-independent bet on CFET, insulated from the mCFET-versus-sCFET outcome.
insights.quote: Both approaches start from the vertical stacking of Si/SiGe layers from which the n and pFETs are fabricated.
insights.locator: Imec and its industrial partners are working

insights.claim: imec's new backside contacting module produced a fivefold improvement in bottom pFET drive current versus the conventional integration scheme, demonstrated at 2026 VLSI.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: A 5x drive current gain is the kind of step change that moves CFET from research curiosity to roadmap commitment — a leading indicator for backside-processing equipment orders.
insights.quote: The new scheme results in a fivefold improved drive current (Is) of bottom pFET devices compared to results achieved with the conventional integration scheme.

insights.claim: Access resistance for the bottom pFETs was reduced from 1753 to 378 ohm-micron under imec's new backside contact scheme, and survival yield of the bottom pFETs rose from 45% to 85%.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Yield nearly doubling on the hardest device in the stack is the practical gate on CFET manufacturability — track this metric as the CFET readiness gauge.
insights.quote: the survival yield of the bottom pFETs increased from 45% to 85% compared to previous reported results

insights.claim: The key enabler is a frontside-formed backside dielectric isolation structure created early in the flow by adding an extra Ge-rich SiGe layer that is later replaced with dielectric, which stops the bottom SiGe:B source/drain from being seeded by the underlying Si substrate.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: The fix is a sacrificial-epi-layer trick rather than exotic new tooling, which lowers the adoption barrier and favors incumbent epi and deposition suppliers.
insights.quote: The frontside BDI formation step hence does not add much to the process complexity.
insights.locator: A key element of the new module

insights.claim: The conventional backside-only BDI approach fails on three counts — variability in bottom SiGe:B source/drain volume, wasted space that raises access resistance, and yield loss factors on the backside contacts that work against industrial adoption.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Names the three defect mechanisms that would have stalled CFET; each is a discrete process-control opportunity for metrology and inspection vendors.

insights.claim: Backside contacting delivers benefits beyond resistance — it enlarges the process window for top-device source/drain formation, provides a lever for reducing standard cell height, and decreases routing congestion in the frontside BEOL.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Backside processing is a multi-benefit lever, which is why it will be adopted broadly at advanced nodes and drives demand for wafer bonding, extreme thinning and backside litho.
insights.locator: An improved module for backside contacting

insights.claim: Overall backside process optimization involving wafer bonding, extreme wafer thinning and backside contact etch contributes to the superior pFET performance, meaning the result depends on a full backside toolchain rather than a single new step.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: CFET pulls through an entire backside processing equipment stack — bonders, thinning/grinding, and specialized etch — not one incremental tool.
insights.locator: A key element of the new module

insights.claim: Although demonstrated on a monolithic CFET test vehicle, imec believes the improved backside contact flow is generic and applicable to sequential CFET devices as well.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Path-independent process modules de-risk supplier investment — the module retains value whichever CFET flavor foundries choose.
insights.quote: the process flow is believed to be generic – applicable to sCFET devices as well
insights.locator: While the improved backside contact module

insights.claim: In advanced nanosheet devices the space between stacked nanosheets is too tight for meaningful gate metal thickness variation, which kills the conventional work-function-metal approach to multi-threshold-voltage tuning and forces a volume-less alternative.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: A structural reason why dipole engineering and atomic-layer precision materials displace metal-thickness recipes at GAA and CFET nodes — a shift in materials spend.
insights.quote: the space in between the stacked nanosheets is extremely tight, leaving little room for gate metal thickness variation

insights.claim: Dipole-based multi-Vt tuning works by inserting a shifter material such as lanthanum between the SiO2 interlayer and the HfO2 high-k layer, with different La concentrations producing different threshold voltages without consuming extra volume.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Rare-earth shifter precursors and ALD process control become a differentiated consumable at angstrom nodes.
insights.quote: dipole-forming metal such as lanthanum (La) atoms is added between the SiO2 interlayer and the HfO2 high-k dielectric layer of the gate stack

insights.claim: The industry-standard dipole-last approach is incompatible with CFET because its high-temperature anneal conflicts with the low-temperature replacement metal-gate process CFET devices require.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Thermal budget is the hidden constraint that forces re-tooling of gate-stack recipes at CFET — an under-appreciated source of process-development cost and schedule risk.
insights.quote: the high thermal budget presents challenges for CFET-based devices that implement a low-temperature replacement metal-gate process

insights.claim: imec's earlier dipole-first approach avoided the high-temperature anneal but patterning the La-oxide shifter layer damaged the underlying SiO2 interlayer and degraded device performance, illustrating that the two obvious options each fail on a different axis.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Shows why gate-stack integration schemes take years to converge — useful context for discounting optimistic CFET timelines.
insights.quote: patterning the La-oxide shifter layer was observed to induce damage to the underlying SiO2 interlayer, affecting the performance of the device

insights.claim: The new dipole-middle scheme deposits the shifter on a first thin HfO2 layer that both permits lock-in via a mild anneal and protects the SiO2 interlayer during patterning, keeping total thermal budget below the dipole-last approach especially when multiple shifter materials are integrated.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: A concrete unlock for multi-Vt libraries at CFET nodes, which designers need to serve both HPC and ultra-low-power blocks on the same die.
insights.quote: This thin layer of HfO2 also protects the underlying SiO2 interlayer during shifter patterning.

insights.claim: The dipole-middle demonstration on a CFET test vehicle produced only a small but consistent nFET threshold voltage reduction of about 30mV versus a reference where the La-oxide was removed before lock-in, and only top nFETs were electrically accessible for evaluation.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: A 30mV shift on a partially instrumented vehicle is proof of mechanism, not of a production multi-Vt library — the gap between demonstration and manufacturability is still wide.
insights.quote: The electrical data showed a small but consistent nFET Vt reduction of about 30mV compared to a reference where La-oxide was removed prior to lock-in.
insights.locator: The dipole-middle approach was successfully demonstrated

insights.claim: Ideal devices need different threshold voltages within the same integrated circuit to balance high performance computing against ultra-low power operation, so multi-Vt capability is a design requirement rather than a process nicety.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Explains why a process module with a 30mV demonstrated shift matters commercially: without multi-Vt, one die cannot serve both AI compute and low-power blocks.

insights.claim: CFET enablement rests on two complementary R&D tracks running in parallel — CFET-specific process module development and DTCO exploration of scalable standard cell configurations — so process readiness alone will not deliver the node.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: EDA and library development must run years ahead of process qualification; DTCO capability is a competitive moat for foundries and tool vendors alike.
insights.quote: the development of CFET-specific process modules, and a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) exploration of scalable standard cell configurations

insights.claim: imec's forthcoming DTCO work presents a novel scalable sequential-CFET architecture supporting both split-gate and common-gate device options, which it identifies as key to advancing both the logic and SRAM scaling roadmaps.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: SRAM has been the worst-scaling block at recent nodes; a CFET split-gate path to SRAM scaling would directly affect cache-heavy AI and CPU die cost.
insights.quote: A novel scalable architecture for sequential CFET is presented that enables split-gate and common-gate device options, key in advancing both the logic and SRAM scaling roadmaps.

insights.claim: BEOL routability is called out as a separate limiting factor on CFET standard cell scaling, with a dedicated DTCO study needed to demonstrate improved routing to support it.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Interconnect, not the transistor, may become the binding constraint on cell height — keep watch on BEOL metallization and routing-aware place-and-route tooling.

themes.theme: European pilot line and industrial policy

insights.claim: The reported CFET results were achieved within the imec-hosted European NanoIC pilot line targeting beyond-2nm systems-on-chip, with CFET selected as one of its key enabling technologies for extending the logic roadmap into the angstrom era.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Europe is buying an option on the post-nanosheet node through pilot-line funding rather than volume fabs — the leverage point for EU semiconductor policy sits in R&D, not capacity.
insights.quote: CFET development... has been selected as one of the key enabling technologies for extending the logic roadmap into the ångström era

insights.claim: The NanoIC pilot line is jointly funded by the Chips Joint Undertaking through the EU's Digital Europe and Horizon Europe programs and by six participating states — Belgium (Flanders), France, Germany, Finland, Ireland and Romania — making CFET progress a directly state-subsidized output.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific funding vehicles whose renewal or cuts would alter the pace of leading-edge device research outside the US and Asia.
insights.locator: This work has been enabled in part

insights.claim: imec explicitly frames the CFET work as helping Europe remain at the forefront of next-generation semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, positioning device-architecture leadership as the continent's strategic lever rather than fab capacity.
insights.speaker: Cassie Sheng
insights.so_what: European strategic value in semis concentrates in research consortia and tooling (imec, ASML-adjacent ecosystem), not in leading-edge production share.
insights.quote: This will help Europe to remain at the forefront of next-generation semiconductor innovation and manufacturing.
